papers.title: Exclusive photoproduction of $π^0$ up to large values of Mandelstam variables $s, t$ and $u$ with CLAS
papers.authors: M. C. Kunkel, 32, 18 M. J. Amaryan
papers.abstract: Exclusive photoproduction cross sections have been measured for the process $γp \rightarrow pπ^0(e^+e^-(γ))$ with the Dalitz decay final state using tagged photon energies in the range of $E_γ = 1.275-5.425$ GeV. The complete angular distribution of the final state $π^0$, for the entire photon energy range up to large values of $t$ and $u$, has been measured for the first time. The data obtained show that the cross section $dσ/dt$, at mid to large angles, decreases with energy as $s^{-6.89\pm 0.

papers.title: Supersymmetry anomalies in new minimal supergravity
papers.abstract: We determine the general structure of quantum anomalies for the $R$-multiplet of four dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric quantum field theories in the presence of background fields for an arbitrary number of Abelian flavor multiplets. papers.title: A Typology of Data Anomalies
papers.abstract: Anomalies are cases that are in some way unusual and do not appear to fit the general patterns present in the dataset. Several conceptualizations exist to distinguish between different types of anomalies. However, these are either too specific to be generally applicable or so abstract that they neither provide concrete insight into the nature of anomaly types nor facilitate the functional evaluation of anomaly detection algorithms. candidate_claims.description: This CLAS Collaboration paper presents experimental measurements of exclusive π⁰ photoproduction cross sections spanning s = 1.81–3.33 GeV² and large momentum transfer values. It identifies a paradox: measured cross sections greatly underestimate QCD-based GPD predictions while agreeing with constituent counting rules at fixed t/s (~s⁻⁶·⁸⁹ vs. s⁻⁷) and Regge models elsewhere. The paper catalogs theory-experiment discrepancies across multiple regimes. Relevance depends on whether round_7_anomalies:2 addresses exclusive meson production, GPD applications, or QCD scaling anomalies; if so, this work is directly bearing evidence.

It identifies a paradox: measured cross sections greatly underestimate QCD-based GPD predictions while agreeing with constituent counting rules at fixed t/s (~s⁻⁶·⁸⁹ vs. s⁻⁷) and Regge models elsewhere. The paper catalogs theory-experiment discrepancies across multiple regimes. Relevance depends on whether round_7_anomalies:2 addresses exclusive meson production, GPD applications, or QCD scaling anomalies; if so, this work is directly bearing evidence.
